claims.claim_text_normalized: Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) achieve state-of-the-art single-model results on the COCO detection benchmark without bells and whistles.
claims.evidence_quote_short: our method achieves state-of-the-art single-model results on the COCO detection benchmark without bells and whistles

claims.claim_text_normalized: FPN significantly increases Average Recall (AR) by 8.0 points for bounding box proposals over a single-scale Faster R-CNN baseline.
claims.evidence_quote_short: FPN significantly increases the Average Recall (AR) by 8.0 points

claims.claim_text_normalized: FPN improves COCO-style Average Precision (AP) by 2.3 points over a strong single-scale baseline of Faster R-CNN on ResNets.
claims.evidence_quote_short: it improves the COCO-style Average Precision (AP) by 2.3 points

claims.claim_text_normalized: The FPN-based Faster R-CNN system runs at 6 FPS on a GPU.
claims.evidence_quote_short: our method can run at 6 FPS on a GPU

claims.claim_text_normalized: FPN can be trained end-to-end with all scales and used consistently at train/test time, which is memory-infeasible with image pyramids.
claims.evidence_quote_short: our pyramid structure can be trained end-to-end with all scales and is used consistently at train/test time, which would be memory-infeasible using image pyramids

claims.claim_text_normalized: Removing top-down connections in FPN significantly degrades accuracy for Fast R-CNN.
claims.evidence_quote_short: removing top-down connections (Table 2(d)) significantly degrades the accuracy

claims.claim_text_normalized: FPN nearly doubles the accuracy on small objects for segmentation proposals compared to existing methods.
claims.evidence_quote_short: we nearly double the accuracy on small objects

claims.claim_text_normalized: FPN-based mask proposal generation is substantially faster than existing methods based on densely sampled image pyramids.
claims.evidence_quote_short: Our approach, based on FPNs, is substantially faster
